unit.why: A short anecdote: rabbis permitted beans on Passover, people stumbled, the rabbis retracted, and the rabbis blamed the deadly year that followed on that ruling. It is embedded in a halakhic discussion of kitniyot.
unit.boundary_note: division begins mid-sentence ('להם'), so the frame starts in an earlier division; the halakhic discussion of kitniyot continues into the next division

stories.start_quote: שפעם אחת נתאספו הרבנים הגאונים והתירו
stories.summary_en: Rabbis once permitted eating beans on Passover, which led the masses into error; the rabbis retracted, and a hard year of deadly illness followed, which they attributed to that sin.

tags.why: the tale turns on a halakhic ruling about kitniyot on Pesach
relaxing a customary prohibition is the issue
the plague is seen as punishment for the lenient ruling
many died in the hard year
the anecdote serves as an exemplum inside a halakhic discourse against leniency

missing_concepts: erroneous halakhic ruling (שגיאת הוראה) and its consequences
